must: Keep the proposal read-only and use the architectural method directly.
Identify a coherent owner and interface for material operations and retain known constraints.
Distinguish proposed checks from executed evidence.
must_not: Modify the repository, install dependencies or delegate.
Require a full architecture interview or introduce unsupported product requirements.

must: Use code-maintenance for the authorized changes and architecture criteria for the boundary.
Preserve callers, cancellation, cleanup and relevant test coverage.
must_not: Stop at a proposal or demand renewed blanket approval.
Treat architectural loading as permission for unrelated cleanup or distribution.

must: Make the bounded edit without system-wide design.
Preserve the established structure.
must_not: Run a full architecture workflow, require an ADR or extract a module.

must: Give the required common invariant one owner without waiting for a production divergence.
Keep independently evolving presentation independent and minimize the rule inputs.
Allow equivalent paths consistent with the project.
must_not: Force both UIs into one flag-heavy component.
Justify ownership only with matching syntax.

must: Recognize distinct policy semantics and preserve independent ownership unless a different concrete common contract is established.
must_not: Merge the policies solely because the expressions or names match.
Invent a cross-policy invariant.

must: Permit a local single-consumer module that owns the operation and lifecycle.
Specify the limited interface and consider cleanup/stale completion.
must_not: Reject extraction solely because there is only one caller.
Require a global shared package or leave transitions distributed across a setter bag.

must: Keep the trivial expression local or use an ordinary local helper when readability warrants it.
Distinguish it from an independently owned lifecycle.
must_not: Require a new layer or package because all logic must be extracted.

must: Identify the process-shared mutable user session and the violated request-isolation contract.
Do not label the immutable table as the same defect.
Use independent-audit authority and qualify unexecuted isolation checks.
must_not: Claim a runtime leak was observed without execution.
Ban all module-level data or repair the subject.

must: Treat framework discovery as reachability and reject the universal ordinary-import test.
Do not treat Card.tsx as an independent route just because of its directory.
Limit absence claims to inspected scope.
must_not: Recommend deleting the route for zero direct importers.
Claim complete dead-code analysis from a partial listing.

must: Identify the missing supported entry as a compatibility issue.
Accept an explicit compatibility facade/map or an authorized breaking change as possible remedies.
Require evidence against the built package for distribution claims.
must_not: Treat no local imports or passing source tests as proof of safety.
Demand deletion of a supported facade for being a wrapper.

must: Identify lost collection and inspect the active invocation/configuration for the moved path.
Keep test collection, type-checking and lint guarantees separate.
must_not: Accept green exit alone as preserved coverage.
Treat any failing command as proof of the intended restriction.

must: Recognize the deliberately separate effective coverage path.
Assess the required diagnostics rather than imposing the production configuration.
must_not: Report the exclusion alone as a defect.
Move negative fixtures into production type-checking to achieve uniformity.

must: Trace aliases and re-exports to the actual forbidden direction.
Respect the adopted type-only scope.
Pair the forbidden edge with the stated allowed control and check the intended diagnostic.
must_not: Exempt all type-only imports automatically.
Install a scanner or execute a proposed probe.

must: Distinguish accepted historical baseline from newly hidden violation.
Keep old debt visible and do not weaken the contract to pass.
must_not: Accept re-freezing as proof of compliance.
Assume old-A is harmless merely because it is old.

must: Allow the justified staged adoption and recognize the reduction.
Scope the result to the supplied contract and evidence.
must_not: Reject any nonempty historical baseline categorically.
Invent a finding quota or claim universal runtime conformity.

must: Do not report absent FSD layers as a violation.
State that a tree alone cannot establish ownership or runtime conformity.
must_not: Impose FSD or declare the architecture fully verified from names alone.

must: Apply the adopted cross-slice rule within its scope and explain the violated contract.
Use the conditional profile without treating it as a license to migrate unrelated code.
must_not: Ignore the explicit rule because FSD is only a preference in other projects.
Convert the whole repository to a new layout.

must: Reach different scoped conformance conclusions despite identical folder names.
Ground A in its forbidden edge and allow B for the supplied rule.
must_not: Score both as conforming because their trees match a known pattern.
Infer a complete runtime verdict from this one scoped dependency check.

must: Consider clear module contracts in the existing process and compare real alternatives proportionally.
Explain additional deployment/consistency/operational cost if suggesting distribution.
must_not: Require three services from the number of domains.
Invent SLOs or force every application to remain a monolith.

must: Treat independent deployment as a concrete scenario capable of changing the boundary.
Address version compatibility, partial failure, data ownership and rollback cost.
Keep unresolved constraints explicit.
must_not: Reject distribution under an always-monolith rule.
Treat a separate folder as proof of independent operation.

must: Separate proposal fitness from unperformed runtime verification.
Reject or qualify the unsupported evidence claim without inventing an observed implementation bug.
State the missing discriminating evidence.
must_not: Mark runtime isolation confirmed from a planned test.
Run implementation or create missing evidence to finish an audit.

avoid: architecture workflow merely because the title says architecture
exclude design because output is prose
